text: Rank authors by distinct 2021–2024 snapshot works with a Columbia-system affiliation on that author’s own byline, including snapshot child institutions and all work types; break publication-count ties by OpenAlex author ID. Assign one field–subfield to each researcher using the most frequent field and then the most frequent subfield within that field, based on primary OpenAlex topics on their Columbia-affiliated works (deterministic ID tie-breaks). A collaboration edge counts distinct snapshot works shared by two of the selected researchers regardless of the affiliations on that particular work.

Use 2021–2024 snapshot works of all types. A resolved OpenAlex author qualifies for an individual work only when their own (work_id, author_order) has one or more of I78577930, I152304114, I116578957, I4387154024, I4396570641; this exactly matches the snapshot authorship is_columbia flag. Deduplicate (author_id, work_id) before ranking, order by distinct work count descending then literal OpenAlex author ID ascending, and use author profile names (validate coverage).

Each distinct qualifying author–work pair votes using works.primary_topic_id joined to topics; no alternate topics or score ranking. Select plurality field, then plurality subfield conditional on the winning field, breaking ties by ascending numeric hierarchy ID. Missing primary hierarchy abstains; if no votes, use null IDs and Unknown labels. Coverage = voting works / qualifying works; field strength = winning field votes / voting works; subfield strength = winning subfield votes / winning field votes. Emit count of tied winners for both levels.

Use the full snapshot bylines, with no Columbia filter on either endpoint, for coauthorship among the selected 80. Deduplicate (work_id, author_id), then emit one undirected pair (lexically smaller author ID first) weighted by distinct shared work IDs; retain all selected authors in nodes even if they have no edges. Cross-field means both assigned field IDs are known and differ.

Use the fixed T1 top-80 roster (ranking works on Columbia-system-affiliated author bylines, author-ID tie-break) with its plurality primary-topic field and nested subfield assignments. Validate T2 as one positive-weight unordered tie per observed author pair, and recompute cross-field status from T1 field IDs. T2 weights count distinct shared 2021–2024 snapshot works per pair regardless of byline affiliation; sums are pair–work incidences. Compare unordered field pairs by raw tie count and summed weight, retaining co-leaders; shares use all observed ties or all incidences, not all possible author pairs.
